He sat on the edge of his bunk with a stub of pencil and the back of a chart, writing by the light of a lamp that swung with the ship. The others slept; the hull creaked, and now and then a wave struck the plates with a boom he felt in his spine. He wrote slowly, crossing out more than he kept. All his life he had been told that men of his sort did not become writers, and all his life he had suspected they were wrong. Tonight, with the sea black outside and his hand cramped, he felt it more strongly than ever — the certainty that the words were there, if only he were patient enough to find them.
